correctness.rationale: The all-edge exact objective is strictly convex on connected graph allocations, so its optimum is unique and symmetric under S3×S_{n-3}. The three nonzero eigenvalue classes are derived exactly. On the positive face, stationarity yields X^2=n(3(m+1)/r-2m), Y^2=rX^2; the exit thresholds compare as rC-rA=(m^3+4m^2-6m-18)/(2m(m+2)(m+3)), whose sign flips between m=2 and m=3. On remaining faces the full KKT slacks establish 9/5, 45/23, and n(n-2)/((n-3)(n-1)). Symbolic full-matrix spectral checks and numerical full-edge KKT replay passed (3007 counted finite checks). Finite computations are only corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: Seven actual published-finding corpus searches and additional targeted literature searches were compared by graph equivalence and theorem implication. The fully inspected perfect-matching clique theorem has only two price orbits and no unmarked complementary class; the fully inspected complete-tripartite theorem has a different base graph with no within-part edges. Both apply the same general convex method, but neither asserts or implies the two K5 boundaries or the n>=6 disappearance of the exceptional phase. Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi establish the convex problem and equal-price complete-graph endpoint, not these heterogeneous triangle tariffs. The analytic KKT calculation is genuinely additional, though unindexed antecedents cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The marked triangle is a natural minimal nonmatching surcharge motif with three inequivalent edge classes. Its exact all-budget graph-design phase diagram has a motivated structural surprise: on K5 an ordinary-cost edge becomes zero at r=9/5 while the more expensive triangle edges remain active until r=45/23; on every K_n with n>=6 this support cascade is impossible. This nontrivial comparison of which actual links are purchased is not a mere numerical constant or a fixed-topology resistance table, and is useful in understanding network sparsification under heterogeneous marginal costs.
